grammarFocus: 否定、比较、数量范围和时态；限定词的含义。 Teach the new rule in Chinese, then provide at least 8 distinct grammar questions in new sentences. Distinguish a newly taught form from revision. All main reading/listening question prompts and options must be English, with short A0/A1 English prompts. Chinese explanations are allowed. title: Week 41 Listening: Comparing Explanations in a Research Discussion
instructions: 本材料为模拟练习，不是官方雅思试题，也不代表任何分数。先听录音（或阅读 transcript），完成 10 道听力题。注意：录音中有自然插话、修正和干扰信息，答案不会直接朗读。然后学习语法讲解，完成 8 道语法题。最后进行口语和写作迁移练习。所有题目和选项均为英文，解释为中文。
transcript:
Maya: Okay, let's start. The question is why the community garden's volunteer numbers dropped last spring. We have three possible explanations on the table. Ben, you looked at the sign-up sheets. What did you find?

Ben: Right. So, I counted the names on the paper sign-up sheets from March, April, and May. In March there were forty-two names. In April, thirty-one. In May, only nineteen. That's a big fall. But I want to say one thing: the paper sheets were kept in the shed, and the shed was locked for two weeks in April because the lock broke. So some people may have signed up online instead.

Maya: Good point. So the paper numbers might not show the full picture. Priya, you checked the online system. What did you see?

Priya: The online sign-ups actually went up in April. There were twelve in March, twenty in April, and eighteen in May. So if we add paper and online together, the total was fifty-four in March, fifty-one in April, and thirty-seven in May. The drop is smaller than the paper numbers suggest, but it's still there, especially in May.

Ben: Wait, I should correct myself. I said the shed was locked for two weeks. Actually, it was locked for ten days, not two weeks. Sorry. But the point is the same: the paper record has a gap.

Maya: Thanks for the correction. Now, explanation one is the weather. Sam, you had the weather data?

Sam: Yes. Last spring was unusually wet. In April there were eighteen rainy days, compared with nine in a normal April. In May there were fifteen rainy days. The garden is outdoors, so wet weather could reduce volunteer turnout. But I want to be careful: rainy days don't always mean fewer volunteers. Some people don't mind rain. And the garden has a small covered area.

Maya: So weather is possible, but not proven. Explanation two?

Priya: Explanation two is that the garden changed its opening hours. From April, the garden opened at ten in the morning instead of eight. If many volunteers used to come before work, that change could explain the drop. But when I looked at the volunteer comments, only three people mentioned the opening time. Most comments were about something else.

Ben: What were most comments about?

Priya: Most were about the new volunteer coordinator. People said she was hard to reach by phone. But that's not one of our three explanations, so I'm not sure we should add it now.

Maya: Let's keep it as a note. Explanation three is the coordinator. Sam, you looked at that?

Sam: I did. The previous coordinator left in March. The new coordinator started in April. In April and May, the coordinator's phone was answered on only about half the days. So volunteers who called might not have reached anyone. That could explain some of the drop. But I can't say it explains all of it. The numbers don't prove cause.

Maya: Right. So where are we? The total volunteer numbers fell from fifty-four to thirty-seven between March and May. The paper record has a gap because the shed was locked for ten days. Online sign-ups rose in April but fell in May. Weather was wetter than normal, but we can't show that rain caused fewer volunteers. The opening time changed, but few volunteers mentioned it. The coordinator was harder to reach, and that is a possible factor. But none of these explanations is proven by the data alone.

Ben: So what do we recommend?

Maya: I think we should say: the drop is real but smaller than the paper sheets suggest. The most likely factor is the coordinator's availability, because it matches the timing and the comments. Weather and opening hours are possible but less supported. And we need better records next year, with paper and online counted together every week.

Priya: Agreed. And I'll add the note about the coordinator's phone.

Sam: One more thing. We should not say the coordinator caused the drop. We can only say she may have contributed. The data are not strong enough for more than that.

Maya: Exactly. Let's write that.

grammar.title: 否定、比较、数量范围和时态；限定词的含义
grammar.explanation: 本课重点：1) 否定词 not 的位置和含义：not 否定其后的内容，如 The numbers don't prove cause（数字不能证明因果关系）。2) 比较：smaller than, less supported, harder to reach 表示程度差异。3) 数量范围：only three, most comments, about half the days 表示数量多少或范围。4) 时态：过去时（dropped, was locked）谈过去事实；现在完成（have contributed）谈可能影响；情态动词 may/might 表示不确定。5) 限定词：the 指特定对象，a/an 指一个，some 指一些，all 指全部；限定词改变范围，如 some of the drop 与 all of the drop 不同。
grammar.example: The drop is smaller than the paper numbers suggest, but it's still there, especially in May.

questions.evidence: That could explain some of the drop.
